title: What to Know About the AI-Triggered Cybersecurity Crisis
summary: PHP, a technology that underpins up to 70% of the world's websites, is under threat after a critical memory-handling flaw dubbed PHP2Shell was disclosed that could let attackers take control of affected systems. The US cybersecurity agency CISA urged companies to patch immediately or take vulnerable systems offline, and the tech industry is racing to deploy fixes.

title: Meta's Hunt for AI Capital Strikes a Raw Nerve on Wall Street
summary: Meta's search for new capital to fund its AI buildout unsettled investors, contributing to a sharp market reaction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 2.6%, while Treasury yields recorded their biggest drop since 2023.

title: Cyber Investors Don't Know What to Do With Their AI Worries
summary: AI is creating new security risks and lifting demand for protection, but it also exposes cybersecurity stocks to swings in sentiment around the technology. Shares of the five largest US cybersecurity companies all fell by double digits last week, far outpacing the broader selloff, before some began recovering losses.

title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion to New Mexico in Data Privacy Case
summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta Platforms to pay the state $25 billion, weeks after a jury found the company deceived users about its data-privacy practices, its efforts against hate speech and misinformation, and its handling of a third-party app tied to the 2018 Cambridge Analytica breach. Meta's chief legal officer said he is confident the company will prevail on appeal.

title: SpaceX Takes Conglomerate-Building to Sci-Fi Extremes
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that Elon Musk's mix of businesses under SpaceX will be a maze for investors to evaluate. The piece frames the company's expanding set of ventures as conglomerate-building taken to an extreme.

title: SB Energy Considers Waiting Until December or Later for an IPO
summary: SB Energy is weighing postponing its IPO to December or even next year, later than its earlier September target. The delay adds to signs of a stalled IPO market.

title: Datadog Offered to Buy Security Startup 'Upwind' For Nearly $4 Billion
summary: Datadog has offered close to $4 billion to acquire Upwind, a cloud security startup, according to The Information. The offer would be a major push by the observability vendor into cloud security.

title: Salesforce Wants a Fee Every Time an AI Agent Touches Its Software
summary: Starting around November, Salesforce plans to require customers to register external AI agents, such as Claude, as a step toward charging a fee for each action an agent takes in its apps. Atlassian, Workday, ServiceNow and Datadog are building similar tollgates as software vendors test whether agent fees can offset a possible decline in per-seat subscription revenue. Some consultants say customers may move data outside Salesforce to avoid the charges, and pricing has not yet been announced.

title: Utopai Becomes a Unicorn as Video AI Takes Off
summary: Utopai, a four-year-old AI film studio, has reached a valuation of $1 billion or more, and investors are reportedly already offering up to three times that. The deal highlights strong investor appetite for video AI.

title: Nokia and Nvidia Say AI-RAN Hype Is Justified as Nokia Touts Q3 AI Gains
summary: Nokia CEO Justin Hotard pointed to a boom in AI and cloud product sales in Q3 and said the vendor is well placed for growing infrastructure demand. Nokia and Nvidia executives told the MWL Podcast that close to 20 operators are lined up for lab and commercial AI-RAN trials.

title: AT&T CEO Stankey Argues Scale Matters in Satellite Direct-to-Device
summary: On the Q3 earnings call, AT&T CEO John Stankey outlined the advantages he sees over a potential SpaceX direct-to-device service. He cited AT&T's larger holdings of low-band spectrum, its scaled network and its ability to serve customers inside buildings.

title: Zuckerberg Claims Muse Agent Has Hit 10M Users
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on the Q3 earnings call that the company plans to expand its Muse personal agent and charge businesses for transactions it handles. He said the agent has reached 10 million users.

title: RBC's AI Chief Sounds the Alarm Over AI Agents
summary: Bruce Ross, RBC's AI chief, says the bank is concerned about letting AI agents access customer accounts and move money without the right safeguards in place.

title: The Signal Chats That Cost OpenAI Researchers Their Jobs
summary: OpenAI fired three safety researchers for mishandling sensitive information after security officers examined their phones and found some had enabled disappearing messages on Signal chats with an external AI-safety researcher. The researchers had reportedly been pushing to keep the workings of AI systems visible and to let outsiders examine them.

title: Meta's Muse Is Going Gangbusters. But Where Is the Payoff?
summary: Meta's Muse AI agent has reached 10 million downloads in a little over a month since launch. The piece asks how that adoption will translate into revenue at a time when investors are scrutinizing Meta's AI spending.

title: A Veteran of the Telecom Bust Navigates the AI Boom
summary: Ciena CEO Gary Smith, who lived through the telecom bust of the early 2000s, describes himself as suitably paranoid but optimistic about demand for optical networking gear driven by AI data-center build-outs. The profile frames how a survivor of the last infrastructure cycle is managing the current one.

title: The Best Boards in America Are Helping Drive AI Strategy
summary: The WSJ Leadership Institute's Best Boards 2026 ranking of S&P 500 companies shows top boards, including those at Lam Research, eBay, Trimble, Lumentum and Nasdaq, playing an active role in AI strategy. Common traits include directors with technology expertise, dedicated technology committees and dashboards that track AI metrics such as agents deployed and AI-generated revenue.

title: SK Hynix Scraps U.S. IPO of Flash-Memory Unit Solidigm
summary: SK Hynix shelved plans for a U.S. public offering of Solidigm, which had aimed to raise roughly $10 billion to $15 billion, citing market conditions and share-price trends. It is the latest listing pulled amid fears of an AI bubble, following Australian data-center operator Firmus Grid's cancelled IPO earlier this month.

title: AI Rout Hits Tech Stocks as Nasdaq Posts Worst Day Since June
summary: The Nasdaq composite fell 2.6% on Thursday, its worst day since June, with Meta down 7% and the PHLX semiconductor index off 6.7% as data-center-linked stocks from Alphabet to Amazon also dropped. Premarket trading on Friday suggested the selloff might find a floor for now.

title: Cyber Chiefs Face Stark Options to Fix Global PHP Security Flaw
summary: A flaw dubbed PHP2Shell lets attackers steal data from web servers and launch attacks on site visitors, leaving companies to either bolster defenses and race hackers or take sites offline. Amazon researchers saw exploitation four days before public disclosure, and there is no easy fix, with remediation and recovery costs mounting.

title: Chinese Hackers Spied on Thousands of Companies After Breaching ConnectWise
summary: Hackers linked to China's government spied on about 2,250 companies after stealing credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service, according to Microsoft researchers. ConnectWise shut the service down to investigate and expects to restore it by the end of the weekend, while Microsoft said AI agents helped the attackers attempt nearly 3,000 sign-ins a minute.

title: Lasers, Robots and AI: The Fight to Save Salmon Goes High-Tech
summary: Salmon producers such as Mowi are deploying AI cameras, net-cleaning robots and blue-light lasers that zap sea lice to cut losses in ocean pens. About 14% of farmed Atlantic salmon in Norway died before maturity last year, and demand from health trends, sushi and weight-loss drugs is pushing the industry toward technology to improve survival.

title: Instacart Is Exploring a Sale
summary: The Information reports that Instacart has been in talks to sell itself, a move that could end a 14-year run as an independent company.

title: VC Firms Tap LP Pools, Warehouse Loans for Speedy AI Cash
summary: Venture capital firms are using new financing methods, from warehouse loans to inviting limited partners to co-invest, to keep pace with the ballooning size of AI startup funding rounds.

title: Ramp Investors Went Nuclear Against Airwallex After Doomed Deal
summary: Investors in fintech Ramp reacted aggressively against rival Airwallex after a deal between the two companies collapsed, according to The Information. The article details the fallout from the failed transaction between the payments and spend-management startups.

title: SpaceX Eyes 80,000 US Cell Sites for Starlink Mobile
summary: SpaceX is reportedly in talks with tower companies to secure access to at least 80,000 US sites as it advances plans for a nationwide mobile network to rival AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile US.

title: CCS Insight Predicts SpaceX Buys an Operator and Apple Leads 6G Devices
summary: Analyst firm FDM CCS Insight published bold predictions for 2027 and beyond, including that SpaceX acquires a mobile operator and Apple leads 6G device launches.

title: UAE-Led Operation Identifies $39 Billion Linked to AI-Enabled Fraud
summary: A UAE-led international operation targeting AI-enabled fraud and cross-border scam networks identified more than $39 billion in funds and cryptocurrencies linked to scam activity.

title: AI Hacks Are Coming Thick and Fast and Overwhelming the Internet
summary: Criminals are adopting next-generation, AI-powered hacking tools, and a serious internet flaw has triggered a wave of attacks that the WSJ dubs "Black October." The volume and speed of AI-enabled intrusions is straining defenders across the internet.

title: Anthropic's Margin is OpenAI's Opportunity
summary: OpenAI's push to undercut Anthropic on price is showing results. At HR software firm Rippling, Anthropic models handled 57% of engineers' coding work in May versus 16% for OpenAI; that has since reversed to 52% OpenAI and 18% Anthropic as the company sought to cut costs, according to CEO Parker Conrad.

title: Disclosure Day: Anthropic's Breakneck Growth Meets a Long List of Risks Ahead of Mega-IPO
summary: As Anthropic prepares for a mega-IPO, WSJ reports the company is generating very rapid revenue growth but faces risks including a narrow customer base and uncertain access to the computing power it needs. The Information's nightly Briefing adds that the public S-1 could land as early as Monday and is expected to clarify profitability, cash flow, partner payments to Google and Amazon, revenue concentration, founder voting control (a planned 50.1% combined) and lockup terms.

title: Meta's Unending AI Spending
summary: Meta said it will keep spending aggressively on AI and is creating a new class of nonvoting stock to help fund it, then disclosed roughly $825 billion in future leases and noncancelable contracts. Shares fell nearly 8%, and despite record third-quarter revenue the company reported negative free cash flow, leaving it reliant on advertising to pay for its data-center build-out.

title: Jassy Says AWS Is 'Largely Sold Out' of Compute Through Next Year as Hyperscaler Earnings Loom
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast that AWS is largely sold out of computing capacity through the end of next year, and called the Annapurna Labs acquisition possibly Amazon's best deal ever. Google and Microsoft report on Wednesday and Amazon on Thursday, with any change to data-center spending plans or AI demand forecasts likely to move jittery markets.

title: The Biggest Takeaways From Anthropic's IPO Prospectus
summary: The Wall Street Journal pulls out what stood out in Anthropic's S-1 filing, from the potential for its models to help cure cancer to a large cushion of cash. The filing also discloses risk factors, including the possibility that humans lose control of AI models.

title: The Bull Case for AI Armageddon
summary: A WSJ piece aimed at investors weighing the Anthropic share offering argues that even a 10% chance of human extinction from AI could amount to a 90% win for a portfolio. It frames the expected-value case for owning the stock despite the existential risks the company itself discloses.

title: Stripe's AI Shopping Lead Puts Card Giants on Edge
summary: As AI shopping assistants such as Instinct and Meta's Muse gain traction, Stripe has taken a leading position in how the agents pay, often through one-time-use virtual cards. That leaves card networks with less control over the shopping and payment process, and people close to the card firms say it has Visa and Mastercard on edge. Both have built their own agent-payment technology that uses customers' existing cards, but it remains at an early stage.

title: Salesforce Customers Brace for New Fees to Use Claude in Its Apps
summary: Salesforce plans to require companies to register the outside AI agents they use inside its apps, possibly as soon as next month, and customers expect new fees as a result. Consultants say some customers are already rethinking how they use tools like Claude. The move is part of a broader shift in which software makers look for ways to charge for AI agent access.

title: Datadog Offered to Buy Security Startup Upwind for Nearly $4 Billion
summary: Datadog is back at the table to acquire Upwind, a cloud security startup that monitors AI agents, after talks between the two fell apart last year. The offer, reported at nearly $4 billion, raises questions about how to value companies in this corner of the security market.

title: The Argument in Favor of Tranched Rounds
summary: The Information makes the case that tranched funding rounds, in which capital is committed in stages rather than all at once, make sense for capital-intensive AI startups. The piece by Stephanie Palazzolo looks at why this structure suits companies with very large up-front compute needs.

title: Pentagon Probes Possible Refrigerator Hacks at Six U.S. Military Sites
summary: U.S. Army and Pentagon investigators are examining outages of refrigeration systems at military commissaries, after hackers took down similar systems at French grocery stores. Six sites were affected, including F.E. Warren Air Force Base, Fort Huachuca, Fort Irwin, Travis Air Force Base, Naval Station Newport and Columbus Air Force Base.

title: PwC Confirms Breach at Third-Party Vendor Holding Employee Training Records
summary: PricewaterhouseCoopers said employee learning records were compromised in a cyberattack on a third-party vendor that stores them for the firm. The Everest hacking group has claimed it stole 590 gigabytes of PwC data.

title: Moonshot AI Curbs Hacking Capabilities of New Kimi Model
summary: China's Moonshot AI said it has reduced the offensive cybersecurity capabilities of its latest model as concerns grow over AI-powered attacks. The Beijing-based startup plans to release the open-weight Kimi K3.1 Pro by Nov. 4.

title: This German Energy Giant Is an Overlooked AI Bargain
summary: WSJ's Heard on the Street column argues that Siemens Energy is an overlooked way to play AI-driven power demand. The column notes the German company is outselling GE Vernova on gas turbines, the equipment central to data center power build-outs.

title: Verizon Bags $2B AWS Deal, Hails Efficiency Drive
summary: Verizon announced an agreement worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services to supply dark fibre infrastructure to meet AI workload demand. The operator also reported third-quarter results showing a spike in post-paid customer additions.

title: VMO2 Lauds AI Impact on RAN
summary: Virgin Media O2 reported an improvement of around 20% in spectral efficiency from using AI in its radio access network during a test with Nokia at a busy transport hub. The result adds to operator evidence on the practical gains from AI-RAN.

title: Canada Faces a Satellite-Launch Crunch as SpaceX Retires Its Workhorse Rocket
summary: Investors are asking Canadian satellite companies how they will reach orbit as SpaceX retires its workhorse rocket. Canada's homegrown launch vehicles are expected to be years away from offering an alternative.

title: Two Thirds of Tracked Telco AI Deployments Now Live, GSMA Intelligence Says
summary: GSMA Intelligence's Telco AI State of the Market report for Q3 2026 finds AI commercialisation continuing to accelerate, with two thirds of the AI deployments it tracks across the telecoms sector now live. The report also notes high capex growth among hyperscalers including AWS, Microsoft and Google.

title: Microsoft Is Trying to Shed a Lot of Workers. Just Don't Call It a Layoff
summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees in the U.S., Canada, India and the U.K., more than a quarter of its 223,000-person workforce. An April voluntary retirement offer to roughly 8,600 staff drew acceptance from more than 30%, and a person familiar with the matter says far fewer are expected to accept this time. The move is part of a broader push by big tech to pare headcount while funding AI.

title: Why Anthropic's Rivals Are Rooting for Its IPO
summary: WSJ argues the Anthropic listing, likely within weeks and seeking up to $100 billion, will signal how open capital markets are to every other AI player. AI-linked stocks have fallen over the past month, CoreWeave is down more than 35%, and big tech is expected to sell about $250 billion of bonds this year and $400 billion next. Meta, which needs funding for roughly $200 billion of next-year capex, and OpenAI, which is eyeing its own IPO next year, both have a stake in a strong debut.

title: Broadcom CEO Intervened to Seal $63 Billion Anthropic Debt Deal
summary: Broadcom and a bank consortium arranged a $63 billion financing, the largest AI-infrastructure debt deal to date, to fund chips for Anthropic. A special-purpose vehicle buys chips designed by Broadcom and Google and made by TSMC, then leases them to Anthropic, whose payments service the debt. Broadcom guaranteed much of the debt and accepted higher interest rates to keep banks on board, and the deal closed as Anthropic filed for its IPO.

title: Nvidia to Invest $3 Billion in Meta's Equity Offering as They Expand AI Partnership
summary: Meta plans to raise as much as $95 billion in equity to fund its AI build-out, starting with a $37.5 billion first step anchored by Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. Nvidia will put in $3 billion and Meta will deploy more Nvidia infrastructure for next-generation AI agents. Meta had flagged the raise in its latest earnings and said timing matters before rivals saturate funding options.

title: Anthropic Says Enterprise AI Adoption Remains in 'Early Phases'
summary: A WSJ review of Anthropic's roughly 400-page S-1 finds heavy concentration in technology and software development, with roots in financial services, law and pharmaceuticals. A case study says orders placed through Walmart's Sparky assistant, built on Anthropic models, are 35% higher in value than those without it. The column sets this against Apollo economist Torsten Slok's finding that firms outside tech see little AI payoff, and says the go-to-market challenge is growing.

title: Anthropic's 'Adjusted' Profit Exposes Wall Street's Earnings Game
summary: WSJ looks at how Anthropic's reported results differ from adjusted figures, noting its losses were the flip side of large gains booked by investors Amazon and Alphabet. The S-1 shows an $80.7 billion first-half net loss that largely reflects an accounting adjustment tied to financing agreements, while operating loss narrowed to $693 million from $2.1 billion a year earlier.

title: How Florida Took the Lead in Battling Big Tech
summary: Florida, led by Gov. Ron DeSantis and Attorney General James Uthmeier, is pursuing a multi-front effort to rein in AI model development, protect consumer privacy and shield minors from social-media harms. The push is gaining momentum in other states as public sentiment turns against data centers and worries grow about uncontrolled AI agents and job disruption.

title: CISA Issues New Strategy to Refocus the Agency
summary: CISA's Monday road map, issued after eight years of unclear priorities, narrows the agency to three goals: ejecting adversaries from federal and critical-infrastructure systems, hardening against the most disruptive threats rather than all hazards, and a distributed approach combining private-sector and state resources. Acting Director Nick Andersen said physical and cyber security can no longer be treated separately. The plan does not address budget and staffing cuts that lawmakers and analysts say have hampered the agency since 2025.

title: Chinese AI Tool Linked to Hacks in Japan
summary: Around 80 Japanese firms were targeted in attacks bearing digital traces of Artex, an AI agent developed in China, according to cybersecurity firm Ierae; eight occurred in the past month. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi convened an emergency cabinet meeting and ordered countermeasures by the end of the week, with the cybersecurity minister to work with allies to attribute the attacks.

title: The Four Places Where the Midterms Will Decide the Fate of Data Centers
summary: Data-center developers are watching next week's elections nervously, as dozens of local ballot measures and races could add moratoriums and restrictions. Candidates from both parties in states including Texas, Ohio, Michigan and Georgia have proposed pauses, stricter rules or less generous tax breaks, driven by concerns over power prices and water use.

title: Anthropic Moves to Lock In Enterprise Customers
summary: Anthropic's S-1 shows net revenue retention of 900% as of Sept. 30 and about 11,900 enterprises spending $100,000 or more in the past year, up more than 12 times. It also shows more enterprises signing non-cancelable annual or multiyear contracts with minimum commitments, which fits its $657 billion compute leasing commitments. OpenAI is winning cost-sensitive customers with cheaper models, but Anthropic's Opus 5.5 release showed capability still dominates buyer choice.

title: Why Anthropic's 85% Margin Is a Reality Check for Skeptics
summary: The Information reports that Anthropic's filing shows it running its models far more efficiently than a year ago, with margins around 85% according to the headline figure. The piece argues the compute-efficiency gains should make skeptics of AI unit economics rethink their math.

title: Ex-GitHub CEO Launches Entire, a Coding Repository Built for AI Agents
summary: Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke launched Entire, a code-hosting product built for AI agents, with features to track what coding agents do and why. The startup has raised $60 million from Felicis and others. It targets customers frustrated by months of GitHub outages earlier this year.

title: Verizon CEO Plays Down SpaceX Threat
summary: Verizon CEO Dan Schulman pushed back on concerns about SpaceX's proposed direct-to-device mobile service. He warned SpaceX would face years of construction and hundreds of billions of dollars in spending to build a rival terrestrial network.

title: An Obscure Data Standard Is the Latest Open Banking Holdup, and an Unlikely Political Hot Potato
summary: The Financial Data Exchange standard is the most widely used technical standard for financial data sharing in North America, but Ottawa has questions about its American roots. The issue is emerging as a new obstacle to Canada's open banking rollout.

title: SpaceX Lines Up Record $40 Billion GPU Financing With Apollo
summary: SpaceX agreed a $40 billion financing with an Apollo Global Management-managed entity to lease GPUs for its data centers, the largest GPU financing to date. It is reportedly structured through an off-balance-sheet special purpose vehicle that could shield its credit rating. Elon Musk said debt markets have closed to companies earning only from AI data centers and predicted consolidation among 200+ neoclouds, while Apollo's chief economist noted zero financial payoff from AI outside tech.

title: DoorDash in Exclusive Talks to Acquire Instacart
summary: Semafor reported DoorDash is holding exclusive talks to acquire Instacart. The Information first reported on Friday that Instacart was exploring a sale and had held preliminary talks with DoorDash and Uber.
